ApprovedMetadataRecord.description: The project's metadata record as a person approved it: the version named by the last approval of a metadata_record document in the project (docs/specs/projects.md). A drafter treats what it holds as supplied, given by a person (docs/specs/drafting.md).

version_ref.description: The version, by its document and number.

media_type.description: The media type of document_text, such as text/markdown or application/json.

conforms_to.description: The schema or profile document_text follows, such as a repository's metadata schema.

document_text.description: The content of the document, as text; a structured record is serialised.

ApprovedMetadataRecord.title: ApprovedMetadataRecord

Assurance.description: How the harness came to know the principal (docs/specs/policy-and-identity.md).
Assurance.title: Assurance

ChoiceAnswer.description: The researcher's answer to the choice question the turn before asked: the values they chose and any text they gave in place of an option. The app checks it against that question before it sends the turn (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

answer_to.description: The invocation whose reply asked the question.

answer_values.description: The values of the options chosen; empty when the researcher answered in their own words.

answer_other.description: The researcher's own answer, given in place of an option where the question allows it.

ChoiceAnswer.title: ChoiceAnswer

ChoiceOption.description: One option of a choice question.

option_value.description: What the agent reads back when the option is chosen. A string, never a number: a number reaches the agent as a floating-point value over A2A.

option_help.description: One sentence that helps the researcher tell this option from the others.

ChoiceOption.title: ChoiceOption

ChoiceQuestion.description: A question with a fixed set of options that a conversational agent asks the researcher in its reply, to be answered by choosing rather than typing. One or several options may be chosen, and where question_other is true the researcher may answer in their own words instead. Option values are unique within the question. Asking never suspends the run: the researcher may ignore the question and type (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

question_prompt.description: The question, as a short line a person reads before the options.

question_options.description: The options, in the order they are shown; between 2 and 12, with unique values.

question_multiple.description: True when several options may be chosen; one only otherwise.

question_other.description: True when the researcher may answer in their own words instead of an option.

ChoiceQuestion.title: ChoiceQuestion

ConversationTurn.description: One earlier turn of a conversation, as the caller presents it to the agent. An agent turn names the agent and version that produced it and the invocation it came from.

turn_text.description: What was said in the turn.

turn_agent_id.description: For an agent turn, the agent that produced it.

turn_agent_version.description: For an agent turn, the version of the agent that produced it.

turn_invocation_id.description: For an agent turn, the invocation it came from.

ConversationTurn.title: ConversationTurn

CurrentVersion.description: The version of a project document that a drafter is to regenerate: the document's latest, its text, and its state with the reason a person gave for any decision on it (ADR-0036 decision 7). A drafter that regenerates it names version_ref in its payload's revises.

version_ref.description: The version, by its document and number.

document_title.description: A short name a person can tell documents apart by, such as README for raw/.

media_type.description: The media type of document_text, such as text/markdown or application/json.

document_text.description: The content of the document, as text; a structured record is serialised.

version_state.description: Whether a person has approved or rejected the version, or not yet decided.

decision_reason.description: The reason the person gave for their decision, in their words. Present for a rejection, and for an approval only if they gave one.

CurrentVersion.title: CurrentVersion

Delegation.description: One child invocation an agent in grounding mode delegation made through the harness (docs/specs/orchestration.md). Recorded by the conductor from its own run of the child, never reported by the agent. content_hash is the dd-envelope-json-v1 hash of the child envelope, which is what a relayed reply cites.
Delegation.title: Delegation

Document.description: The payload of an agent that drafts or regenerates a project document: a metadata record, a README, a data dictionary or another document, as text (docs/specs/projects.md). The only payload class that becomes a project document.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

document_title.description: A short name a person can tell documents apart by, such as README for raw/.

media_type.description: The media type of document_text, such as text/markdown or application/json.

conforms_to.description: The schema or profile document_text follows, such as a repository's metadata schema.

document_text.description: The content of the document, as text; a structured record is serialised.

revises.description: The version this document replaces, when an agent regenerates it. Absent for a new document, for which the conductor mints a document_id.

document_questions.description: The questions this version asks the researcher, one for each gap it leaves. A README marks each gap with the HTML comment <!-- dd:gap question_id -->; a data dictionary leaves the cell empty and its source unknown.

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).

Document.title: Document

DocumentKind.description: What a project document is for (docs/specs/projects.md).
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

DocumentQuestion.description: A question a drafter asks the researcher about one gap in the version it drafted: a README section it could not write, or a data dictionary cell it could not fill. The target is either gap_section, or gap_file, gap_field and gap_column together. question_id is derived from the target, so it is the same in every version that leaves the same gap (docs/specs/drafting.md).

question_id.description: The question's identifier within its document: q- and 16 lower-case hexadecimal digits, derived from the gap it targets.

question_prompt.description: The question, as a short line a person reads before the options.

gap_section.description: The heading of the README section the question would fill, as the drafter wrote it.

gap_file.description: The path of the file whose data dictionary row the question would fill.

gap_field.description: The field whose data dictionary row the question would fill.

gap_column.description: The data dictionary column the question would fill, such as unit.

DocumentQuestion.title: DocumentQuestion

DocumentVersionRef.description: One version of a project document: the document the conductor minted an identifier for, and the version's number within it, counted from 1.

document_id.description: The identifier the conductor minted for the document, a UUIDv7.

version.description: The number of a version within its document, counted from 1.

DocumentVersionRef.title: DocumentVersionRef

DraftAnswer.description: A person's answer to one question a version of the document asked (DocumentQuestion). The drafter places answer_text, as given, in the gap or cell the question names and marks it supplied (docs/specs/drafting.md).

answered_question.description: The question_id of the question answered.

answer_text.description: The answer as the person gave it.

DraftAnswer.title: DraftAnswer

DraftRequest.description: What a drafter is asked for: a project document of one kind, drafted from the project's facts (docs/specs/projects.md). Every agent that returns a Document accepts it, so an agent that drafts a document can replace another without its caller changing. The project's facts are the inventory, the requirements of the repository chosen, the metadata record a person approved last and, to regenerate a document, its current version with any decision on it. In a project, the conductor puts the inventory, the requirements and the metadata record in from the project, replacing whatever the caller sent, so a caller leaves them out; outside a project, the caller sends them. Filling current_version is TODO(#394). The answers a person recorded to the current version's questions are filled in by the conductor in the same way (docs/specs/drafting.md).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

document_kind.description: The kind of document to draft.

inventory.description: The project's inventory, the latest added. In a project the conductor fills it; a caller leaves it out.

requirements.description: The requirements of the repository chosen last. In a project the conductor fills it; a caller leaves it out.

metadata_record.description: The project's metadata record, the version a person approved last, if any has been. In a project the conductor fills it; a caller leaves it out.

current_version.description: The document's latest version, when the drafter is to regenerate it. Absent for a new document.

draft_answers.description: The answers a person recorded to the current version's questions. In a project the conductor fills them; a caller leaves them out.

DraftRequest.title: DraftRequest

Envelope.description: The agent's response. Every field an agent did not decide (identifiers, timestamps, telemetry, the policy applied, the human it acted for) is filled by the conductor, so an agent cannot mislabel its own run. Conditional rules not expressible in JSON Schema are enforced by contract.validate: failed or suspended requires problem; abstained or referred requires outcome.reason_code; succeeded requires payload; a payload requires payload_schema, and payload_schema a payload.

invocation_id.description: UUIDv7 (RFC 9562), time-ordered so the append-only store sorts without an index.

agent_id.description: Stable identifier of the agent, e.g. advisor.standards or stub.abstain.

grounding_mode.description: The grounding contract the agent declared and the linter applied. Filled by the conductor from the agent's specification, never by the agent.

policy_bundle_ref.description: The institutional profile the conductor applied, as profile:<profile_id>@v<version>. The deployment chooses the profile; a request cannot name one (docs/specs/policy-and-identity.md).

policy_digest.description: SHA-256 of the profile file's bytes, so a stored run names exactly the rules applied.

acting_for.description: The human this invocation acted for. Filled by the conductor from the authentication boundary, never from the request; a delegated invocation acts for its parent's (docs/specs/policy-and-identity.md).

contract_version.description: The version of this core contract the conductor governed the invocation under (docs/specs/contract.md).

input_schema.description: The digest of the class schema the input was checked against, as the agent's card carried it. Absent when the agent does not accept the input's class (docs/specs/contract.md).

payload.description: Agent-specific payload; absent unless the outcome is succeeded. An instance of the payload class the agent declares, named by schema_class; every payload class mixes in Grounded. The class schema the agent's card carries checks the rest (docs/specs/contract.md).

payload_schema.description: The digest of the class schema the payload was checked against, as the agent's card carried it. Present exactly when there is a payload; the run store keeps the schema under this digest, so a stored run renders with the schema it was checked against (docs/specs/contract.md).

requires_human_review.description: Always true (C13, C15). Emitted as a constant so no consumer can produce an envelope claiming otherwise.

conversation_id.description: UUIDv7 shared by every turn of one conversation. On a child invocation, the parent's.

project_id.description: UUIDv7 of the project the invocation belongs to (docs/specs/projects.md). Set only by the conductor, from the conversation the request is a turn of or, on a child invocation, from the parent's grant; a caller's request that carries it is refused. Never sent to the agent.

parent_invocation_id.description: The invocation that delegated this one. Set only by the conductor, from a delegation grant; a caller's request that carries it is refused.

delegations.description: The child invocations this invocation delegated to, in the order they ran.

Envelope.title: Envelope

EvidenceItem.description: The retrieved content a grounding claim rests on, identified by a hash over its canonicalised projection (not the HTTP body).

snapshot_ref.description: Which copy of the registry answered, e.g. snapshot:2026-09-04 or live.

content.description: The document the named canonicalisation turns into bytes, already projected, so that a reader or the linter (E1) can recompute content_hash from the envelope alone (docs/specs/grounding.md). Where a payload cites this item from grounded_on, this is what the citation identifies.

EvidenceItem.title: EvidenceItem

FileInventory.description: The facts about a dataset's files that the project holds in place of the files (docs/specs/projects.md): for each file its path, size, digest and format, and for a table its fields. Made by a command run where the data live; it never contains a file's content. advisor.files reads it.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

inventory_files.description: Every file under the dataset's root folder that the command read, sorted by path.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

inventory_identified_with.description: What identified the formats, such as fido 1.6.1 with PRONOM signatures v109, or that only file extensions were used.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

FileInventory.title: FileInventory

Grounded.description: Mixed into every payload class and every item class that asserts an identity. The linter walks a payload document for grounded_on lists and never needs to know the payload class; a payload that lacks grounded_on at its root is a violation, not a pass.

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).

Grounded.title: Grounded

GroundingMode.description: The grounding contract an agent declares. The linter applies a rule set per mode (docs/specs/grounding.md); an envelope always records which one applied.
GroundingMode.title: GroundingMode

GroundingRef.description: The identity and content hash of one retrieved thing a payload rests on. The only way a payload may name an external resource as a decided identity, and the only place it names it: what the reference identifies is read from the evidence item with the same source_id and content_hash (docs/specs/grounding.md). The linter matches every GroundingRef against a retrieval span on both fields.
GroundingRef.title: GroundingRef

IdentificationMethod.description: How a file's format was identified, from strongest to weakest (docs/specs/projects.md).
IdentificationMethod.title: IdentificationMethod

Input.description: Any input: an object that names its class in schema_class. The core checks nothing else; the class schema of the agent's accepted input class does (docs/specs/contract.md).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

Input.title: Input

InventoryFile.description: One file of a dataset, as the inventory command found it.

file_path.description: The file's path relative to the dataset's root folder, with forward slashes. Never an absolute path, which would say where the data live.

file_sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the file's bytes, in lowercase hex, by which the file deposited can be shown to be the file described.

file_media_type.description: The file's media type (MIME type), when it could be told.

file_pronom_ids.description: Every PRONOM unique identifier (PUID) the file matched, such as fmt/95 or x-fmt/18. More than one means the identification is ambiguous; none means the format is unknown.

file_identified_by.description: How the PRONOM identifiers were arrived at.

file_fields.description: For a table, its fields as a Frictionless Table Schema inferred from a sample of rows.

InventoryFile.title: InventoryFile

InventorySummary.description: What the inventory a project holds is, without its files: the conductor fills it into a Message so that the agent knows the project has one (docs/specs/projects.md).

inventory_digest.description: The inventory's dd-input-json-v1 hash, by which the project keeps it.

inventory_file_count.description: How many files the inventory lists.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

InventorySummary.title: InventorySummary

InvocationRequest.description: What the conductor hands to an agent. One request produces exactly one Envelope. A conversation is the set of top-level invocations sharing a conversation_id; each turn is one request and one envelope (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

invocation_id.description: UUIDv7 (RFC 9562), time-ordered so the append-only store sorts without an index.

agent_id.description: Stable identifier of the agent, e.g. advisor.standards or stub.abstain.

requirement_ids.description: Blueprint or project requirement identifiers the invocation is exercising.

conversation_id.description: UUIDv7 shared by every turn of one conversation. On a child invocation, the parent's.

project_id.description: UUIDv7 of the project the invocation belongs to (docs/specs/projects.md). Set only by the conductor, from the conversation the request is a turn of or, on a child invocation, from the parent's grant; a caller's request that carries it is refused. Never sent to the agent.

parent_invocation_id.description: The invocation that delegated this one. Set only by the conductor, from a delegation grant; a caller's request that carries it is refused.

input.description: What the agent is asked to work on: an instance of one of the input classes the agent accepts, named by schema_class. The class schema the agent's card carries checks the rest (docs/specs/contract.md).

InvocationRequest.title: InvocationRequest

Message.description: One conversational turn addressed to an agent: the text of the turn and the conversation so far. The history is part of the input, so the input hash covers everything the agent saw. In a project that holds an inventory, the conductor adds what it is (docs/specs/projects.md); in any project, it adds the entry point chosen and the progress the project log shows (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

message_text.description: What the user said in this turn.

history.description: The earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first.

project_inventory.description: The inventory the conversation's project holds, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds no inventory.

choice_answer.description: The researcher's answer to the choice question the previous turn asked, when they answered by choosing. message_text still carries the answer as prose.

project_entry.description: The Blueprint entry point (1, 2 or 3) the researcher chose for the conversation's project, the latest chosen. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or none was chosen.

project_progress.description: The process-flow steps the conversation's project log shows started, done or skipped, in flow order. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project. Derived from the log on every turn, never stored.

Message.title: Message

ModelCall.description: One call an agent made to a language model, as the agent reports it (docs/specs/disclosure.md). model_id is the model the provider's response named, which may be more exact than the one configured. prompt_digest identifies the messages sent: the harness keeps them beside the run, never in the envelope, and checks that they hash to it.

model_provider.description: Who serves the model, as the agent's card names it (anthropic).

called_at.description: When the agent sent the call.

prompt_digest.description: SHA-256 of the prompt sent, as dd-prompt-json-v1: the JSON object of what the agent sent besides sampling parameters (system prompt, messages, tools), keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8 (dd_sdk.prompts).

ModelCall.title: ModelCall

Obligation.description: Whether a requirement set's field or document stops a package (docs/specs/deposit.md).
Obligation.title: Obligation

Outcome.description: One class rather than a union of five. The status enum carries the vocabulary; reason_code is required when status is abstained or referred; problem (on the Envelope) is required when status is failed or suspended.

referred_to.description: The human role a referred outcome hands to, e.g. data_steward.

statement.description: A human-readable sentence explaining the outcome (C14).

Outcome.title: Outcome

OutcomeStatus.description: The outcome vocabulary. The Blueprint does not define one; this is the harness's specification contribution.
OutcomeStatus.title: OutcomeStatus

Payload.description: Any payload: an object that names its class in schema_class and mixes in Grounded. The core checks nothing else; the class schema of the agent's payload class does (docs/specs/contract.md).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).

Payload.title: Payload

Principal.description: The human an invocation acted for (Blueprint §5.4), or the accountable human role where it acted for an institution. Named by the deployment's authentication boundary and recorded by the conductor; a request cannot name one, and an agent is never sent one (docs/specs/policy-and-identity.md).

principal_id.description: An absolute IRI for the person or role; an ORCID iD for a person where one exists (P5).

name.description: How the person or role is named to a reader of the record.

assurance.description: How the harness came to know the principal.

vouched_by.description: The IRI of the identity provider's issuer that vouched for the principal, for example https://orcid.org, so that a reader can weigh the claim by who made it. Required when assurance is authenticated and absent when it is asserted (docs/specs/policy-and-identity.md).

Principal.title: Principal

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs, used verbatim for failed and suspended outcomes. The two extension members carry the resumption condition for suspended.

resume_condition.description: What must happen for a suspended invocation to resume (extension member).

resume_after.description: Earliest time a suspended invocation may resume (extension member).

ProblemDetails.title: ProblemDetails

ReasonCode.description: Why an agent abstained or referred. Adapted from the standards-advisor experiment's NothingFoundReason.
ReasonCode.title: ReasonCode

Reply.description: The payload of a conversational agent: the text of its reply. An orchestrator's reply is grounded on its input and on the envelopes of the invocations it delegated to.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

reply_derivation.description: How reply_text came about. template for a rule-based agent, model for a model.

conversation_title.description: A short label a person can tell the conversation apart by, written by a model from the researcher's first message. Set only on a conversation's first turn, and only by an agent that declares it model-derived; absent otherwise.

reply_question.description: A question with fixed options the reply asks, at most one; absent when the reply asks nothing or asks in prose.

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).

Reply.title: Reply

RepositoryRequirements.description: The requirements of the repository a researcher chose: its standard's set with the repository's override, if there is one, merged on top (ADR-0038 decision 2). The harness makes it when the choice is recorded, keeps it among the project's blobs, gives it to the drafters and checks the project against it. Not a set of the deployment's configuration, so it has no requirement_set_id of its own; requirement_sets names the sets it was merged from.

re3data_id.description: The repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100012124.

repository_name.description: What the researcher calls the repository chosen, such as ORDA.

conforms_to.description: The URI of the metadata schema of the standard's set.

requirement_sets.description: The sets the requirements were merged from, the standard's first.

fields.description: The metadata properties the set requires or recommends.

required_documents.description: The document kinds that must have an approved version before a package is built.

recommended_documents.description: The document kinds whose absence is a warning.

media_types.description: An override only: the media types the repository accepts. Empty means any.

max_file_size.description: An override only: the largest file the repository accepts, in bytes.

max_item_size.description: An override only: the largest deposit the repository accepts, in bytes.

licences.description: An override only: the licences the repository offers, each an SPDX identifier or the URL of the repository's own terms.

warnings.description: What the researcher was told when the repository was chosen, such as that it does not list DataCite.

RepositoryRequirements.title: RepositoryRequirements

RequirementField.description: One metadata property a requirement set requires or recommends.

property.description: The schema's property, such as DataCite's titles or types.resourceTypeGeneral.

qualifier.description: Values that narrow the property, such as a subjectScheme. Part of what identifies a field when an override is merged with its standard's set.

schema_org.description: The schema.org term the property maps to, by which the record is read as RDF.

form_label.description: An override only: the label of the repository's deposit form field the value goes in.

RequirementField.title: RequirementField

RequirementSet.description: What a deposit must or should have (docs/specs/deposit.md). A standard's set covers any record in one metadata standard and names it in re3data_names; a repository override adds what one repository asks and names it in re3data_id. The harness merges the two for the repository a researcher chose, checks the project against the result, and gives it to the drafters. Kept as YAML in the deployment's configuration, not sent by agents.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

requirement_set_id.description: Identifies the requirement set, such as datacite-4 or orda.

version.description: The version of the set, raised on every change.

title.description: What a person calls the standard or the repository.

url.description: Where the standard or the repository is described.

conforms_to.description: The URI of the metadata schema. An override names the standard's set it builds on.

re3data_names.description: A standard's set only: the metadataStandardName values in re3data that select it.

re3data_id.description: An override only: the repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100012124.

fields.description: The metadata properties the set requires or recommends.

required_documents.description: The document kinds that must have an approved version before a package is built.

recommended_documents.description: The document kinds whose absence is a warning.

media_types.description: An override only: the media types the repository accepts. Empty means any.

max_file_size.description: An override only: the largest file the repository accepts, in bytes.

max_item_size.description: An override only: the largest deposit the repository accepts, in bytes.

licences.description: An override only: the licences the repository offers, each an SPDX identifier or the URL of the repository's own terms.

guidance.description: The pages the set's values were taken from, so that a steward can check them.

RequirementSet.title: RequirementSet

RequirementSetUse.description: One requirement set a choice of repository was merged from, as the deployment held it.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the set's file, in lowercase hex.

RequirementSetUse.title: RequirementSetUse

StepProgress.description: How far one step of the Blueprint's process flow has gone, as the project log shows it: started, done or skipped. A step the list leaves out is open (docs/specs/orchestration.md).
StepProgress.title: StepProgress

StepState.description: How far a process-flow step has gone; a step with none of these states is open.
StepState.title: StepState

TableField.description: One field of a tabular resource, mirroring a Frictionless Table Schema field descriptor. Frictionless publishes no RDF namespace, so these slots carry see_also rather than a slot_uri (TODO(#20): revisit if Frictionless publishes term IRIs).

field_type.description: Frictionless field type (string, number, integer, boolean, date, datetime, time, duration, geopoint, ...).

TableField.title: TableField

Telemetry.description: Run measurements. The energy slots exist so P14 can be populated later without a schema change; at v0 they are null and not_measured.

trace_id.description: OpenTelemetry trace identifier, 32 lowercase hex characters.

model_calls.description: Each call to a language model the agent made during the run, in the order made. Absent for an agent that called none.

Telemetry.title: Telemetry

TurnRole.description: Who spoke in a conversation turn.
TurnRole.title: TurnRole

VersionState.description: The state of one version of a project document (ADR-0035 decision 6). Every version begins proposed; once approved or rejected, it does not change.
VersionState.title: VersionState

description: What the conductor hands to an agent. One request produces exactly one Envelope. A conversation is the set of top-level invocations sharing a conversation_id; each turn is one request and one envelope (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

invocation_id.description: UUIDv7 (RFC 9562), time-ordered so the append-only store sorts without an index.

agent_id.description: Stable identifier of the agent, e.g. advisor.standards or stub.abstain.

requirement_ids.description: Blueprint or project requirement identifiers the invocation is exercising.

conversation_id.description: UUIDv7 shared by every turn of one conversation. On a child invocation, the parent's.

project_id.description: UUIDv7 of the project the invocation belongs to (docs/specs/projects.md). Set only by the conductor, from the conversation the request is a turn of or, on a child invocation, from the parent's grant; a caller's request that carries it is refused. Never sent to the agent.

parent_invocation_id.description: The invocation that delegated this one. Set only by the conductor, from a delegation grant; a caller's request that carries it is refused.

input.description: What the agent is asked to work on: an instance of one of the input classes the agent accepts, named by schema_class. The class schema the agent's card carries checks the rest (docs/specs/contract.md).
